Anna / Karthik — attaching a redline of our standard DPA with clarifying notes on the UK addendum/IDTA approach. High-level notes here before you dig in:

- SCCs: we ship a standard SCC addendum when customers require EU->US transfers. That addendum documents processor-subprocessor relationships, technical safeguards, and the fallback routing logic.
- UK addendum / IDTA: we have an explicit UK addendum that mirrors the EU flow but includes an IDTA equivalence statement; where customers require additional assurances, we offer a limited onshore-cache option (ops-supported) and a bridging letter for transitional states.
- TIAs/DTIAs: we can provide a sample TIA packet (redacted telemetry + KV-cache mapping + service-level routing statement). Note: some telemetry artifacts are sensitive and provided under an NDA; we can provide a certified sample set instead.

Open items I need from Proteus: whether your procurement will accept the bridging letter + onshore-cache SOW (if requested) or insist on full IDTA execution up-front. That choice affects timing.

I've attached: redwood_dpa_redline_20250729.docx (redline + comments) and a short FAQ on UK addendum behavior.
